# Bhūmija Sutta (MN 126 (PTS MN iii 138))

**ID:** MN 126 (PTS MN iii 138)

**Title (Pali):** Bhūmija Sutta

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhūmija Sutta* ("With Bhūmija", MN 126; PTS MN iii 138) is the 126th discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* [SuttaCentral]. Set at the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels' Sanctuary near Rājagaha, the narrative commences when the venerable Bhūmija visits the residence of Prince Jayasena [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995]. Jayasena questions Bhūmija regarding the assertions of certain ascetics and brahmins who debate whether spiritual success requires making an aspiration or wish [Humphreys 1956; Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995].

The central teaching of the sutta examines the dynamics of spiritual practice, demonstrating that achieving the fruits of the holy life (*phalassa adhigamāya*) does not depend on formulating a wish (*āsa*) or making vows, but on practicing properly and cultivating the appropriate causes [Bodhi 2003; Jackson 1983; SuttaCentral]. Because the path functions causally, living the holy life in a proper (*yoniso*) rather than improper (*ayoniso*) manner via the Noble Eightfold Path naturally brings liberation [Anālayo 2010; Jackson 1983; Khemananda 1993]. The discourse illustrates the fruitfulness of proper practice and the futility of wrong paths through a sequence of similes: attempting to squeeze oil out of gravel rather than sesame seeds, churning water rather than milk for butter, or rubbing dry wood to generate fire [Khemananda 1993; Thanissaro 1996].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include a discourse in the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 173) and a Sanskrit fragment cataloged in the Turfan collection (SHT sutta80) [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus confirms matches with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26.45) as well as links to the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003) and the *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125) [DharmaNexus]. Across Pali literature, DharmaNexus registers matching passages across 118 texts, displaying substantial overlap with the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35), *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), several *Aṅguttaranikāya* nipātas, and related Majjhima discourses such as MN 123, MN 30, and MN 36 [DharmaNexus].
